name: orthorhombic S8 (a constant index)
paper: C. Palache, H. Berman and C. Frondel, Dana's System of Mineralogy, 7th edition, vol. I (1944) 140–144, for the principal indices, as J. W. Anthony, R. A. Bideaux, K. W. Bladh and M. C. Nichols, Handbook of Mineralogy, vol. I (Mineral Data Publishing, 1990) 506, gives them
source: the Handbook of Mineralogy's sulphur sheet, https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/sulphur.pdf, SHA-256 a443e6a2a44e77f4bd5c9c6a70bbbda1a019c0c9294bc2c9538c045886fe39a3, fetched 2026-10-14: the principal indices n_α = 1.9579, n_β = 2.0377 and n_γ = 2.2452 at the sodium D lines, for the room-temperature crystal. No open visible dispersion of S8 was found: refractiveindex.info, Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation and HITRAN's aerosol list hold none, and Sasson et al. 1985 (Icarus 64, 368, DOI 10.1016/0019-1035(85)90061-2) is closed
licence: three published principal indices, cited as facts; no data set is copied (decision-r08-t5d ruling 5)
reduction: a constant index: the principal indices averaged in the dielectric function for randomly oriented grains, n = √((n_α² + n_β² + n_γ²) ÷ 3) = 2.0838, at every wavelength of 380–780 nm, with k = 0. Sulphur's dispersion (its indices rise towards the blue) and its blue absorption edge are not drawn, so an S8 haze draws too white in the blue
standIn: a constant index: crystalline S8's principal indices at 589 nm averaged for randomly oriented grains, 2.084 with no dispersion and k = 0, since no open visible optical constants of S8 were found; its blue absorption edge is not drawn
